description:
This is a short accessible / low-mobility trail to a small picnic area and a fishing dock along the northern shoreline of Sheridan Lake, near Loon Bay Resort and the popular Interlakes Centre.

In addition to an accessible trail, there is also an accessible pit toilet in the parking lot. The accessible trail from the parking lot to the fishing dock and picnic area is less than 330 meters in length. The old trail does continue past the dock and picnic area and connects over to Texas Road at Loon Bay Resort, but this portion of the trail has not been improved and is currently not considered a low-mobility / accessible trail.

Sheridan Lake is a very popular destination for fishing, with rainbow trout and brook trout being the two most popular species targeted by anglers. The lake is known as a premier fishing destination, renowned for its large rainbow trout. The lake is well-stocked, with many rainbow trout reaching trophy sizes. The average size of rainbow trout caught is around 3-5 pounds, but fish exceeding 10 pounds are common, and anglers have even caught and reported fish over 20 pounds.

This short, family-friendly and accessible trail provides an opportunity for visitors without boats to try fishing in this world-class managed fishery.

This trail is constructed and managed as a low-mobility / accessible trail; horses and motorized vehicles are not permitted on the trail. Thank you for your cooperation.
directions:
Trail Head location Lat 51.540376 , Long -120.903535

About 9 km south of 100 Mile House on Hwy 97, turn east onto Highway 24 and follow for about 32 km to Airmail Road, which is a short distance past the Interlakes Centre and Loon Bay Resort. Turn right (south) onto Airmail Road. The parking lot and trailhead is a couple hundred meters down this road and on the right.
